title: Temperature Converter
description: Convert between Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin instantly with the exact conversion formulas.

formula.summary: Unlike length or weight, temperature scales aren't simple multiples of each other, so each conversion pair uses its own linear formula, converting through Celsius as an intermediate step.

faqs.question: Why can't temperature use a simple multiplication factor like other units?
faqs.answer: Celsius and Fahrenheit have different zero points (0°C = 32°F) as well as different scale sizes, so the conversion needs both a multiplication and an addition/subtraction step - a full linear equation, not just a ratio.

faqs.question: What is absolute zero?
faqs.answer: Absolute zero, the coldest possible temperature, is 0 K, which equals −273.15°C or −459.67°F. Kelvin has no negative values for this reason.

seoContent.heading: The three major temperature scales
seoContent.body: Celsius is used by most of the world and defines 0° and 100° at water's freezing and boiling points. Fahrenheit, still standard in the United States, sets those points at 32° and 212°. Kelvin, used in science, starts at absolute zero and uses the same size degree as Celsius, just shifted by 273.15.

seoContent.heading: How the conversion formulas were derived
seoContent.body: The Fahrenheit-Celsius formula comes from matching the two known reference points (freezing and boiling of water) and solving for the linear relationship between them, giving the 9/5 scaling factor and 32-degree offset that every conversion in either direction relies on.
